title: CLI fails to match files on Windows-style backslash paths
description:
On Windows, running the CLI with a backslash-style path (e.g. .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html) fails with "No matching .html or .php files found for: ..." even though the file exists.

Root cause: src/cli.js:66 passes raw argv patterns directly into fast-glob (fg). fast-glob treats backslash as a glob escape character, not a path separator, so a pattern like .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html gets mangled into .\tests\fixturesmastermind-lsparts\footer.html (backslash + following char is consumed as an escape sequence) and never matches.

Repro (confirmed):
- fg([".\\tests\\fixtures\\mastermind-ls\\parts\\footer.html"]) -> []
- fg(["./tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/footer.html"]) -> matches correctly

Reported via: `npm start .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html` and `npx . .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html` both failing.

Suggested fix: normalize backslashes to forward slashes on each pattern before passing to fast-glob in src/cli.js, so Windows-style paths are supported.

title: bun build --compile produces a binary that cannot boot (css-tree createRequire)
description:
`npm run compile` (`bun build --compile`) produces a ~95 MiB executable that cannot start.
Parked: the blocker is in a transitive dependency, not in this repo, and there is nothing
to do here until it changes upstream.

## Symptom

Every invocation fails identically, including `--help`, which does no validation work:

```
error: Cannot find module '../data/patch.json' from 'B:\~BUN\root\wp-block-guard.exe'

Bun v1.4.0 (Windows x64)
```

The failure is at import time, before `argv` is parsed, because
`src/block-runner-adapter.js` imports `block-runner` (and therefore jsdom) at module top
level.

## Cause

```js
// node_modules/css-tree/lib/data-patch.js
import { createRequire } from 'module';
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const patch = require('../data/patch.json');
```

Bun's `--compile` bundler statically analyzes literal `require`/`import` calls to decide
what to embed in the binary's virtual filesystem. A `require` constructed at runtime by
`createRequire()` is invisible to that analysis, so `patch.json` is never embedded, and the
runtime fallback resolves against `$bunfs` (`B:\~BUN\root\...`) rather than a real disk
path.

Under plain Node this works, because a relative CJS require from inside a package bypasses
that package's own `exports` restriction. The failure is specific to `--compile`.

`css-tree@3.2.1` is reached via `block-runner → jsdom → @asamuzakjp/dom-selector →
css-tree`. Three jsdom-side packages dedupe to the same copy (`npm ls css-tree`).

## What works

- `node bin/wp-block-guard.js` — the supported path, unaffected.
- `bun run bin/wp-block-guard.js` (uncompiled) — works correctly, which is what confirmed
  the in-process adapter is sound under Bun's runtime.

Only `--compile` is broken.

## Why this is parked rather than closed

A standalone executable is still a legitimate distribution goal, and the `compile` script
will begin working unchanged the day the upstream pattern changes. Nothing in this repo
needs to be undone or redesigned.

## If picked up

Two routes, neither attempted:

1. A Bun bundler plugin that handles this `createRequire`-indirected JSON require.
2. Patch or pin `css-tree` / `@asamuzakjp/dom-selector` to avoid the pattern.

Before either, re-test on a current Bun: this was measured on Bun 1.4.0, and static
analysis of `createRequire` is exactly the kind of thing Bun improves release to release.
Also re-check whether `css-tree` still ships the pattern.

Full detail: `handoff/2026-09-03-bun-compile-implementation-report.md` §5.

title: Add source field to finding schema for agent find-and-replace
description:
Add a `source` field to the finding schema so the agent-facing (JSON) output shows the
exact flagged text alongside the existing `fix` advice.

## Field order

In `makeFinding()` (`src/findings.js`), the returned object gains `source` positioned
after `message`, before `fix`:

```js
{ code, severity, file, line, blockName, message, source, fix }
```

`fix` is unchanged — it stays advisory prose for the human operator, it is not
rewritten into literal replacement code.

## What `source` contains, per finding code

| Code | `source` |
|---|---|
| `PHP_HEADER_STRIPPED` | the stripped `<?php ... ?>` header text |
| `PHP_INTERPOLATION_UNCHECKED` | the exact matched `<?...?>` fragment (captured before `maskEmbeddedPhp` blanks it) |
| `STRUCTURAL_UNBALANCED_DELIMITER`, `STRUCTURAL_MISMATCHED_CLOSER`, `STRUCTURAL_INVALID_ATTRS_JSON` | the exact delimiter comment text (`<!-- wp:name {...} -->`), sliced from the token's byte offsets already computed in `tokenizeDelimiters()` (`src/structural.js`) |
| `BLOCK_INVALID`, `BLOCK_RUNNER_WARNING` | the single source line at `item.source.htmlLine`, sliced from `body` in `src/pipeline.js` |
| `BLOCK_RUNNER_SKIPPED`, `BLOCK_RUNNER_FAILURE`, `STRUCTURAL_NO_BLOCKS` | `null` — no single location to point at |

## Touch points

- `src/findings.js` — schema field order, JSDoc for `makeFinding()`'s overrides
- `src/structural.js` — `checkStructuralBalance()` must pass through `start`/`end` (or
  the sliced text) from each token so `pipeline.js` can build `source`
- `src/php-fragment.js` — `scanForEmbeddedPhp()` must return the matched fragment text,
  not just `token` (the opener)
- `src/pipeline.js` — thread `source` into every `makeFinding()` call; for
  `BLOCK_INVALID`/`BLOCK_RUNNER_WARNING`, slice the line from `body` using
  `item.source.htmlLine`

## Also required

- `--json` output (`src/cli.js:129`) picks this up automatically once `makeFinding()`
  returns it — no separate change needed there.
- The human-formatter change to also display `source` is tracked separately (see linked
  bead) since it needs a rendering proposal first.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every finding code above produces the specified `source` value (or `null`) in both
  `br` output and `--json` output.
- `source` text is byte-exact from the input file at that point in the pipeline (no
  re-indenting/trimming beyond what's already inherent to line-slicing).
- Existing tests continue to pass; add/update fixtures covering `source` for at least
  one code from each row of the table above.

title: Spike: does a block validated in isolation match its in-document verdict?
description:
Settle one factual question: **does a block validated on its own get the same verdict as
the same block validated inside its document?**

This is the single unresolved fact standing between "per-block correction is wontfix" and
"per-block correction is cheap and worth doing". It is a spike: produce an answer, not a
feature.

## Why it matters

`wpbg-x8v` (add a `match` field carrying corrected replacement markup) is closed. Its cost
objection is now dead — with the in-process adapter, block-runner calls after the first
cost 11-36ms, so canonicalizing every invalid block in a file is fractions of a second.

What remains is correctness. Every viable design for `match` extracts one block and
canonicalizes it alone, because block-runner only ever returns whole-document output and
reformats untouched blocks in the process. That is only sound if an isolated block
validates the same way it does in context.

## What to test

Use `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html`, which has four `BLOCK_INVALID`
findings at varying nesting depths, including a paragraph two levels inside a group that is
itself invalid.

1. Validate the whole document; record each item's `block`, `status`, and `reason`.
2. Extract each block's span with `tokenizeDelimiters()` (`src/structural.js`) plus an
   opener/closer pairing pass — note `tokenizeDelimiters()` returns a flat token list and
   does no pairing; `checkStructuralBalance()` builds that stack and discards it.
3. Validate each extracted span alone. Compare verdict and reason against step 1.

Report: for how many blocks does the isolated verdict match, and where it diverges, why.

## Specific things to probe

- **Nesting depth.** Two hand-written snippets already agree with their in-document verdict
  (`hero-blob-1` valid alone and in context; `word-cloud-bg` invalid in both), but neither
  had inner blocks and neither came from the tokenizer.
- **A block whose parent is invalid.** The most likely place for divergence.
- **Blocks that inherit context** — `layout`, alignment, or theme-level attributes a parent
  supplies. If a child's `save()` output depends on ancestor attributes, isolation is
  unsound for it specifically, which may mean `match` is viable only for blocks that do not
  inherit.
- **Whether extraction must include the parent's delimiters** to preserve context, and if
  so, whether that reintroduces the overlapping-span problem that makes sequential
  find-and-replace unsafe.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written answer — yes, no, or "yes except for cases X" — with the comparison table it
  came from, recorded in `handoff/` or `archive/`.
- If isolation is sound, reopen `wpbg-x8v` and note the cost figures.
- If it is unsound, add the finding to `docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md`
  so the ADR's "settle that before reopening" line points at a real answer.
- Either way, `wpbg-x8v`'s dependency on this bead is resolved.
close_reason: Answered: isolation matches the in-document verdict unconditionally. save() receives no block context, so validation inputs are intrinsic to the block. Write-up in handoff/2026-09-05-block-isolation-verdict-spike.md

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## Answered: **yes, unconditionally** — isolation matches the in-document verdict

Full write-up, both comparison tables, cost figures and caveats:
`handoff/2026-09-05-block-isolation-verdict-spike.md`.

### The short version

A block sliced at its exact delimiter span and validated alone gets the same verdict *and*
the same reason as it does inside its document. Verified on all 8 blocks of
`tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html` and all 10 of a purpose-built
context-inheritance probe — **0 missing, 0 extra** in both reconciliations.

### Why it holds (this is the load-bearing part)

Not a fixture coincidence. `validateBlock`
(`@wordpress/blocks/build/api/validation/index.cjs:370`) compares exactly two things:

```js
generatedBlockContent = getSaveContent(blockType, block.attributes);
const isValid = isEquivalentHTML(block.originalContent, generatedBlockContent, logger);
```

`getSaveContent` is called with **two** arguments, so `innerBlocks` defaults to `[]` in
`getSaveElement(blockTypeOrName, attributes, innerBlocks = [])`, which calls
`save({ attributes, innerBlocks })`.

**`save()` receives no context parameter.** `usesContext`/`providesContext` is an editor and
server-render mechanism and never reaches `save()`. Ancestor `layout`, `align` or
theme-level attributes therefore cannot influence a descendant's saved markup — which was
this bead's primary suspected source of divergence.

Both validation inputs are intrinsic to the block and survive slicing byte-for-byte.

### The three probes the bead asked for

- **Nesting depth** — depths 0/1/2 all agree, from tokenizer-derived spans rather than
  hand-written snippets.
- **A block whose parent is invalid** — the paragraph at line 8 inside the invalid
  `word-cloud-bg` group: same verdict, same reason.
- **Blocks that inherit context** — `core/columns`/`core/column` (width to `flex-basis`),
  `core/buttons`/`core/button`, `core/list`/`core/list-item`. A deliberately corrupted
  `core/column` is invalid both in document and alone, identically.

### Must extraction include the parent's delimiters?

**No** — so the overlapping-span problem that would make sequential find-and-replace unsafe
does not arise.

### Cost

8 isolated validations = 128ms total (median 9ms); 10 = 29ms total (median 2ms), after the
one-time ~7.9s jsdom/Gutenberg boot already paid by the first call.

### Bearing on other beads

- **wpbg-x8v** — reopen condition met; reopening per this bead's acceptance criteria. Two
  *new* obstacles found that were not known when it was closed: canonicalize decodes HTML
  entities (not byte-preserving), and not every invalid block is repairable.
- **wpbg-djb** — unblocked. The correct item-to-block mapping can now be recovered without
  parsing `reason` prose and without patching block-runner: validate each candidate span to
  learn which blocks are genuinely invalid, then map to `items` in document order.
- **docs/adr/0003** — its "settle that before reopening" line now has a real answer.

title: --fix strips the file's trailing newline
description:
`--fix` rewrites files without their final newline.

## Repro

`tests/fixtures/wp-block-guard/invalid-heading-missing-class.html` ends with `\n`. After a
`--fix` run the rewritten file does not:

```
input      endsWithNewline=true   tail="2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->\n"
after fix  endsWithNewline=false  tail="h2>\n<!-- /wp:heading -->"
```

## Cause

block-runner's canonicalized markup (`report.output`) carries no trailing newline, and
`src/pipeline.js` writes `header + fixedBody` verbatim.

Pre-existing, and **not** a regression from the in-process adapter: the old subprocess
`--out` path and the new `canonicalize()` call were compared on the same input and produce
byte-identical output, trailing newline included (i.e. absent in both).

## Why it is worth fixing

Every file a user fixes gains a spurious one-line diff, and POSIX tooling flags
newline-at-EOF loss. It is noise attributable to this tool, in files the user did not
otherwise change.

## Suggested fix

In `src/pipeline.js`, preserve the input's trailing-newline state when writing the fixed
body: if `raw` ended with a newline and the fixed body does not, append one. Do not
unconditionally append — that would add a newline to files that never had one.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `--fix` run preserves the input file's trailing-newline state, present or absent.
- Regression test covers both directions.

title: Propose colorized/tabular human report format
description:
The human-readable report (`formatHuman()` in `src/report.js`) is plain text with no
color and no tabular layout (unicode markers `✔/✗/⚠/ℹ` only, per
`src/report.js:21-46`). The user has said it is "almost unreadable" and wants a
proposal — not a spec — before any implementation.

## Scope

1. Produce a proposal with 2-3 concrete rendering options (color usage, columnar/table
   layout, grouping by file/severity) for the user to pick from before writing code.
2. Once an option is chosen, also surface the new `source` field (see linked bead) in
   the human output, positioned consistently with the agent JSON (after the message
   line, before the fix line).

## Not yet decided

- Color library/approach (repo has no existing color dependency — check whether one
  should be added or ANSI codes written by hand)
- Table vs. grouped-list layout
- Whether `--json` / non-TTY output should auto-disable color

## Acceptance criteria

- A proposal (with previews) has been presented to and approved by the user.
- Implementation matches the approved option.
- `source` is visible in the human report once the agent-output bead lands.

title: Land or park the in-process block-runner adapter from the bun-inprocess-adapter worktree
description:
The `bun-inprocess-adapter` worktree holds a completed, tested rewrite of
`src/block-runner-adapter.js` that is **not merged** and tracked by nothing. It has stalled
on a goal it cannot reach, but the rewrite itself is independently valuable and at risk of
being lost.

Worktree: `.claude/worktrees/bun-inprocess-adapter` at `f0c8d58`, branch
`bun-inprocess-adapter`, clean tree. Note `.claude/worktrees/` is now gitignored, so the
directory no longer appears in `git status` — this bead is the only thing pointing at it.

## What the worktree contains

`src/block-runner-adapter.js` rewritten from spawning block-runner's CLI as a subprocess to
calling its library API directly (`import { validate, canonicalize } from 'block-runner'`).

- External contract preserved: `validateMarkup()` still returns
  `{ ok, exitCode, data, error, stderr }` and `fixMarkup()` still returns a markup string or
  `null`. No changes were needed in `src/pipeline.js` or `src/cli.js`.
- `exitCode` is synthesized (`report.ok ? 0 : 1`) and `stderr` is always `''`, since a
  library call has neither. Nothing outside the adapter reads either field.
- `canonicalize()` returns the fixed markup on `report.output` — confirmed empirically, not
  just from the `.d.ts`.
- All 37 existing tests pass unmodified, under both Node and plain `bun run`.

Also in the worktree: a `compile` npm script, `bin/*.exe` in `.gitignore`, a README section
on the in-process Layer 2 call, and a `vitest.config.js` comment correction.

Full detail in the worktree's `handoff/2026-09-03-bun-compile-implementation-report.md` and
`handoff/2026-09-03-bun-compile-wp-block-guard-handoff.md`. **Those two files exist only on
that branch** — if it is deleted they go with it, which defeats the purpose `handoff/`
serves.

## Why it stalled

The rewrite existed to make `bun build --compile` viable, and that goal fails for reasons
outside this repo. The compile succeeds (~95 MiB binary) but the binary cannot start, on any
argument including `--help`:

```
error: Cannot find module '../data/patch.json' from 'B:\~BUN\root\wp-block-guard.exe'
```

Root cause: `css-tree@3.2.1` does `createRequire(import.meta.url)` and then
`require('../data/patch.json')`. Bun's `--compile` bundler statically analyzes literal
`require`/`import` calls to decide what to embed in the binary's virtual filesystem, and
cannot see through a runtime-constructed `require`, so `patch.json` is never embedded.
`css-tree` is reached transitively via `block-runner → jsdom → @asamuzakjp/dom-selector →
css-tree`. Fixing it needs a Bun bundler plugin or a patched/pinned `css-tree`, neither
attempted.

Under plain Node and plain `bun run`, everything works. The failure is specific to
`--compile`.

## Why it is worth landing anyway

The adapter rewrite turns out to matter for a reason unrelated to Bun: it makes repeated
block-runner calls essentially free, because the expensive jsdom + `@wordpress/*` boot is
paid once per process instead of once per call. Measured on `develop`'s dependencies:

```
first validate()      8.773s
subsequent validate() 0.014s / 0.011s
canonicalize()        0.012s / 0.022s
```

That is the precondition that makes per-block correction viable, and it invalidates the cost
argument recorded against the `match` field (see wpbg-x8v and
`docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md`, amended). The worktree's own report
concluded "no measurable improvement should be claimed on the performance axis" — correct
for a single CLI invocation, which is all it measured, but not for N calls in one process.

## Suggested resolution

1. Decide the disposition of the branch: merge the adapter rewrite into `develop` on its own
   merits, or keep it parked. Merging is the recommendation — it is tested, contract-
   preserving, and unblocks other work.
2. Either way, **copy the two `handoff/` files onto `develop` first** so the investigation
   survives independently of the branch.
3. Separate the Bun-compile goal from the adapter change. The compile blocker is upstream and
   open-ended; it should not hold the rewrite hostage. Split it into its own bead if it is
   still wanted.
4. Do not commit `bin/*.exe`; the worktree already gitignores it.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `handoff/` reports from this worktree exist on `develop`.
- The branch's disposition is decided and recorded — merged, or explicitly parked with a
  reason.
- If merged: the full suite passes on `develop`, and `README.md` describes Layer 2 as an
  in-process library call rather than a CLI spawn.
- The Bun-compile blocker is either tracked separately or explicitly dropped.
close_reason: Merged into develop as 0aed6de. The in-process adapter landed; follow-ups 1effa87 (stderr capture + regression test, 48 tests passing) and ae04887 (README corrections) complete the acceptance criteria. Bun-compile blocker split out to wpbg-0gu; the handoff reports now live on develop via the merge. Measured effect: block-runner's boot is paid once per run instead of once per file.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** CLI fails to match files when given Windows-style backslash paths

**Current behavior:**
When a user passes a file pattern using Windows-style backslashes (e.g.
`.\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html`) as a CLI argument, the
CLI reports "No matching .html or .php files found" even though the file
exists. This happens because the glob library used to resolve patterns
treats backslash as an escape character, not a path separator, so
backslash-delimited patterns are silently mangled and never match. This
affects `.\`, `..\`, and any other pattern using `\` as a separator, on
Windows only.

**Desired behavior:**
On Windows, file patterns using backslash separators resolve correctly and
match the same files their forward-slash equivalent would, with no manual
conversion required from the user. On non-Windows platforms, backslash
handling is unchanged (it retains its glob-escape meaning there).

**Key interfaces:**
- The function that turns CLI argv into glob patterns should normalize
  path separators (`\` → `/`) per pattern before handing them to the glob
  resolver, but only when running on Windows (`process.platform ===
  'win32'`). Do not normalize on other platforms — backslash is a legal
  filename character and glob-escape character there.
- No change to the glob resolver's matching semantics or its output shape
  (array of matched file paths) is needed.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] On Windows, a pattern like `.\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html`
      resolves to the same file(s) as `./tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/footer.html`
- [ ] Existing forward-slash pattern behavior is unchanged on all platforms
- [ ] A new test passes a raw backslash-style pattern as CLI argv (not
      routed through any existing test helper that pre-normalizes
      separators) and asserts a match on Windows
- [ ] On non-Windows platforms, patterns containing `\` are passed through
      unmodified, preserving glob-escape semantics

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the existing fixture-path test helper that pre-normalizes
  separators for other tests — it serves a different purpose (portable
  fixture paths) and should stay as-is
- Any other cross-platform path handling issues not related to glob
  pattern matching

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## Implementation summary

Fixed the Windows backslash-glob bug at the single call site that matters: `src/cli.js`.

**Change:**
- Added `normalizePatternsForPlatform(patterns, platform = process.platform)` (exported, pure) in `src/cli.js`, just above `main()`. On `win32` it maps each pattern through `p.split('\\').join('/')`; on every other platform it returns `patterns` unchanged.
- `main()` now calls `fg(normalizePatternsForPlatform(patterns), ...)` instead of `fg(patterns, ...)` — the only `fg(`/`fast-glob` call site in `src/` (confirmed by grep), so this is the single choke point, not scattered.

**Why this shape:** fast-glob treats `\` as a glob-escape character, not a path separator, so a Windows-style pattern like `.\tests\fixtures\...\footer.html` gets mangled (backslash + next char consumed as an escape) and never matches. Converting `\`→`/` only on win32 preserves `\` as a legal glob-escape/filename character on POSIX platforms, per the ticket's explicit non-goal.

## Tests added (`tests/cli.test.js`)

1. **CLI-level regression test** (`it.skipIf(process.platform !== 'win32')`): builds the argv pattern as a literal relative backslash string (`'.\\tests\\fixtures\\wp-block-guard\\unbalanced-delimiter.html'`) — deliberately *not* routed through the existing `fx()` helper (which pre-normalizes separators for portability and is out of scope to touch) — spawns the real CLI binary via `spawnSync`, and asserts the backslash run produces the same exit status and JSON report as the forward-slash equivalent. Uses `unbalanced-delimiter.html`, an existing fixture that trips a Layer-1 structural error, so block-runner (Layer 2) is skipped and the test stays fast (no long timeout needed).
   - Used `it.skipIf` rather than an early `if (process.platform !== 'win32') return`, since an early return would report as a *passing* test on non-Windows CI, masking the fact it never ran.
2. **Unit tests for `normalizePatternsForPlatform`**: backslash→forward-slash conversion on `'win32'`, forward-slash patterns left unchanged on `'win32'`, and backslash patterns passed through unmodified on `'linux'`/`'darwin'` (platform injected as a parameter, no `process.platform` mocking needed).

**Red/green verification:** before finalizing, I temporarily reverted the `fg()` call to the pre-fix form and re-ran the new CLI-level test in isolation — it failed (`AssertionError: expected 2 to be 1`, i.e. the backslash run exited 2/"no matching files" while the forward-slash run succeeded), confirming the test actually discriminates. Restored the fix immediately after.

## Full test suite

`npx vitest run` → **47/47 passing** (4 test files) on this run. Note: on two earlier runs, `tests/pipeline.test.js`'s two `--fix` tests (`fixes a near-miss block in place...`, `fixes a file with multiple BLOCK_INVALID findings...`) timed out at 45000ms due to slow/cold block-runner process spawns — this is **pre-existing flakiness unrelated to this change**. I confirmed this by `git stash`-ing my changes and re-running the same test against unmodified `develop` code; it failed identically (same 45000ms timeout). Not touched, per the ticket's stated out-of-scope.

## Files changed
- `src/cli.js` — added `normalizePatternsForPlatform()`, wired into the `fg()` call in `main()`.
- `tests/cli.test.js` — added the regression test and the `normalizePatternsForPlatform` unit tests described above.

## Acceptance criteria checklist
- [x] Windows backslash pattern resolves to the same file(s) as its forward-slash equivalent
- [x] Forward-slash pattern behavior unchanged on all platforms (existing suite unaffected + explicit unit test)
- [x] New test passes a raw backslash-style pattern as CLI argv, not routed through the fixture-normalizing `fx()` helper
- [x] Non-Windows platforms pass `\`-containing patterns through unmodified

title: Add search field to finding schema carrying byte-exact source text
description:
Add a `search` field to the finding schema carrying the **byte-exact source text** of the flagged markup, so an agent-facing (JSON) consumer can locate what to replace without re-deriving positions from prose. `fix` is unchanged — it stays advisory prose for the human operator. `match` (the corrected replacement text) is **out of scope** and tracked separately as wontfix; see "Why `match` is not here" below. ## Field order In `makeFinding()` (`src/findings.js`), the returned object gains one field, `search`, positioned after `message`, before `fix`: ```js { code, severity, file, line, blockName, message, search, fix } ``` ## What `search` contains, per finding code | Code | `search` | |---|---| | `PHP_HEADER_STRIPPED` | the stripped `` header text | | `PHP_INTERPOLATION_UNCHECKED` | the exact matched `` fragment (captured before `maskEmbeddedPhp` blanks it) | | `STRUCTURAL_UNBALANCED_DELIMITER`, `STRUCTURAL_MISMATCHED_CLOSER`, `STRUCTURAL_INVALID_ATTRS_JSON` | the exact delimiter comment text (``), sliced from the token's byte offsets already computed in `tokenizeDelimiters()` (`src/structural.js`) | | `BLOCK_INVALID`, `BLOCK_RUNNER_WARNING` | **`null`** — see "block-runner positions are not usable" below | | `BLOCK_RUNNER_SKIPPED`, `BLOCK_RUNNER_FAILURE`, `STRUCTURAL_NO_BLOCKS` | `null` — no single location to point at | Everything `search` is populated for comes from **our own tokenizer**, never from block-runner. That is the whole reason this bead is cheap: no extra subprocess, no headless-Gutenberg boot, no dependency on block-runner's source mapping. ## block-runner positions are not usable (verified) The original version of this bead specified `search` for `BLOCK_INVALID` / `BLOCK_RUNNER_WARNING` as "the single source line at `item.source.htmlLine`". That was investigated against `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html` and **does not work**, for two independent reasons: 1. **`htmlLine` points at the delimiter comment, never the faulty element.** For all four `BLOCK_INVALID` findings on that fixture, the text needing replacement is the `
`/`

` on the *following* line. Slicing at `htmlLine` yields the `` comment, which is not what is at fault. 2. **Positions are misattributed.** Finding #2 reports `htmlLine: 3` / `offset: 183`, which is the `hero-blob-1` group — confirmed **valid** when validated in isolation — while its `reason` describes the `word-cloud-bg` group at line 6. block-runner appears to map the nth finding of a block name to the nth occurrence of that name in document order, skipping the valid ones. Tracked as its own bug (see linked bead). Emitting a `search` value derived from those positions would hand an agent the wrong text to find and replace, which is worse than emitting nothing. Hence `null` for both codes until the position bug is resolved. ## Why `match` is not here Producing corrected markup requires running the block's `save()` function. WordPress/Gutenberg PR #82013 ("Try: declare block transforms in block.json, read them in the editor and in PHP", open, unmerged, `lib/experimental/`) states this directly in its "What this does not solve" section: > Producing saved markup is a separate problem […] Turning attributes into markup means > running the block's `save()`, which only exists in JavaScript. Empirically confirmed against block-runner: - `validate --json` reports the diff only as prose in `reason` ("Expected attributes [ … ], instead saw [ … ]") — a normalized attribute-tuple diff with no tag name, no quoting and no attribute order. It cannot be turned into replacement text. `--explain` adds nothing to the JSON. - The only real HTML pair ("Content generated by `save` function" / "Content retrieved from post body") appears on **`fix`'s stderr**, for **one** block per run, and only for blocks `fix` could not repair. `validate` writes nothing to stderr. - `fix` reformats the entire document (strips indentation, reorders delimiter JSON keys, drops `"layout":{"type":"default"}`), so a pre/post diff cannot distinguish "was invalid" from "was reformatted" — the verified-valid `hero-blob-1` block changes too. - Some blocks have no `save()`-compatible correction at all (`aria-hidden="true"` on a `core/group`). Upstream's own answer to this is to let a block *declare* it cannot round trip (`serverConversion: false`), not to produce a fix. The only viable route is extracting each block and running `save()` on it one at a time — roughly 12s per invalid block, ~48s for that one fixture. Rejected as disproportionate. ## Touch points - `src/findings.js` — add `search` to the returned object and to `makeFinding()`'s JSDoc, defaulting to `null` when not supplied. - `src/structural.js` — `checkStructuralBalance()` must pass through each token's `start`/`end` on the findings it emits. **Keep its signature unchanged** (it is exported and tested with tokens only); let `runStructuralLayer()`, which already has `content`, do the slicing. - `src/php-fragment.js` — `scanForEmbeddedPhp()` must return the matched fragment text. **Add** a field rather than renaming `token`; `tests/php-fragment.test.js` asserts on `occurrences[0].token`. For an unterminated opener (the fallback loop, no matching `?>` before EOF) there is no fragment to slice — emit the opener text. - `src/pipeline.js` — thread `search` into each `makeFinding()` call. Slice from the **pre-mask** body: structural tokenization runs on the masked body, and `maskEmbeddedPhp` blanks PHP to spaces, so slicing from it is not byte-exact. Masking is length-preserving, so offsets are identical — keep a reference to the body before masking and slice `search` from that. - `src/cli.js` — the per-file `catch` block hand-builds a `BLOCK_RUNNER_FAILURE` finding object, bypassing `makeFinding()`. Either route it through `makeFinding()` or add `search: null` so every finding in the output has the same shape. ## Out of scope - `--json` output (`src/cli.js`) picks `search` up automatically once `makeFinding()` returns it — no separate change needed. - `formatHuman()` (`src/report.js`) is **not** touched here. Surfacing `search` in the human report belongs to the colorized/tabular report bead, which is gated on a rendering proposal. - `--fix`'s current write-the-file behaviour is unchanged by this bead. ## Acceptance criteria - Every finding code in the table above produces the specified `search` value (or `null`) in `--json` output. - `search` text is byte-exact from the file content, sliced from the pre-mask body (no re-indenting or trimming). - Every finding in `--json` output has a `search` key, including the one built by hand in `src/cli.js`'s catch block. - `checkStructuralBalance()`'s signature is unchanged; `scanForEmbeddedPhp()` still returns `token`. - Existing tests pass. Note `tests/structural.test.js` asserts `toEqual([{ code: 'STRUCTURAL_NO_BLOCKS', line: 1 }])` — the one exact-object assertion that adding fields to structural findings will break; update it. Everything else uses `toMatchObject` / `objectContaining` and survives. - Add fixtures covering `search` for **each** populated code — `PHP_HEADER_STRIPPED`, `PHP_INTERPOLATION_UNCHECKED`, and at least one of the three `STRUCTURAL_*` codes — plus one asserting `BLOCK_INVALID` yields `search: null`. - Add a fixture with embedded PHP **inside a delimiter comment's attribute JSON**. This is the only case where slicing from the masked body differs from the pre-mask body, so it is the only test that can catch the pre-mask instruction being ignored. Without it that requirement is unenforced. ## Known limitation of this bead as scoped `BLOCK_INVALID` is the code that fires on real input (all four findings on `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html` are `BLOCK_INVALID`), and it yields `search: null` here because block-runner's positions cannot be trusted — see the linked position bug. So on the markup that motivated this work, the new field is entirely `null`. That is deliberate: emitting text derived from a misattributed position would hand an agent the wrong thing to replace. Visible value for `BLOCK_INVALID` arrives only once the position bug is fixed.

title: Add match field carrying corrected replacement markup
description:
Add a `match` field to the finding schema carrying the **corrected replacement markup**
for a flagged block, so an agent could perform a find-and-replace using `search` (see
linked bead) as the text to find and `match` as the text to write, without the CLI
editing any file.

Recorded and closed as **wontfix**. The reasoning is below so it does not have to be
rediscovered; reopen if the upstream situation changes.

## Why this cannot be done cheaply

Producing corrected block markup means running the block's `save()` function.
WordPress/Gutenberg PR #82013 ("Try: declare block transforms in block.json, read them in
the editor and in PHP" — open, unmerged, `lib/experimental/`) says so directly in its
"What this does not solve" section:

> Producing saved markup is a separate problem […] Turning attributes into markup means
> running the block's `save()`, which only exists in JavaScript.

<https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82013>
Parent issue: <https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/13163>

That upstream work is about HTML→blocks *conversion*, not validation diffs, and is not
usable today in any case. See also
`archive/2026-09-02-wordpress-gutenberg-markup-validation-research.md`.

## What was ruled out empirically

Investigated against `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html` (4 `BLOCK_INVALID`
findings):

1. **Parsing `reason` from `validate --json`.** The diff is present but only as prose —
   "Expected attributes [ [ 'class', … , true ] ], instead saw [ … ]". It is a normalized
   attribute-tuple diff with no tag name, no quoting style and no attribute order, so it
   cannot be turned into replacement markup. `--explain` adds nothing to the JSON.

2. **Scraping the real HTML pair from `fix`.** `fix` does emit genuine markup on
   **stderr** — "Content generated by `save` function" (the correction) and "Content
   retrieved from post body" (the original). But it emits it for **one** block per run,
   and only for a block it could *not* repair. `validate` writes nothing to stderr at all.

3. **Diffing pre/post canonicalization in memory.** `fix` without `--out` is
   non-mutating (input checksum verified unchanged) and prints corrected markup to stdout,
   which looked promising. But it reformats the **entire** document — strips indentation,
   reorders delimiter JSON keys, drops `"layout":{"type":"default"}`, inserts blank lines.
   The verified-valid `hero-blob-1` block changes too, so "changed == was invalid" is
   false and the diff produces spurious pairs.

4. **No correction exists for some blocks.** `aria-hidden="true"` on a `core/group`
   survived `fix` because `save()` will never emit it. Upstream's own answer to this class
   of problem is to let a block *declare* that it cannot round-trip
   (`serverConversion: false`, or `{ "requires": … }`), not to generate a fix. So `match`
   would legitimately be `null` for an unbounded set of real findings.

## The only viable route, and its cost

Extract each block with our own tokenizer and run block-runner on it one block at a time.
That sidesteps the position-misattribution bug (we choose what we send) and gives
element-level, non-overlapping replacements. Cost is roughly 12s per invalid block — about
48s for that single fixture — and it carries an unverified assumption that a block
validated in isolation gets the same verdict as in context, which is doubtful for deeply
nested blocks whose parents are also invalid.

Rejected as disproportionate to the value.

## If this is reopened

- `search` (linked bead) already gives an agent byte-exact text to locate; a human or LLM
  supplying the correction covers most of the original intent without this field.
- The position-misattribution bug (linked bead) must be fixed first — per-block extraction
  needs a trustworthy mapping from a block-runner finding to one of our tokens.
- Check whether block-runner has since gained a structured expected/actual pair in its
  `validate --json` report; that would collapse this to a cheap change.

comments.text:
## Correction to this bead's close reason (2026-09-04)

The close reason on this bead states that per-block canonicalization costs "~12s per
invalid block (~48s for one fixture)" and rejects it as disproportionate. **That figure is
wrong as a general claim**, and cost should not be cited as a reason to keep this closed.

The 12s was measured against `src/block-runner-adapter.js` as it stands on `develop`, which
spawns a fresh block-runner process per call and therefore re-pays the jsdom +
`@wordpress/*` boot every time. Called in-process, the boot happens once:

```
first validate()       8.773s
subsequent validate()  0.014s / 0.011s
canonicalize()         0.012s / 0.022s
```

Per-block correction across a whole file is therefore fractions of a second on top of the
validation the tool already performs — conditional on the adapter calling block-runner as a
library rather than spawning it. That rewrite exists, tested, in the
`bun-inprocess-adapter` worktree; see wpbg-km9, now linked as a blocker.

`docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md` has been amended accordingly.

## What still justifies keeping this closed

The correctness objections are untouched:

- block-runner exposes no per-block correction; `reason` is a normalized attribute-tuple
  diff, not swappable text; `fix`'s stderr yields one pair per run; whole-document
  canonicalization reformats valid blocks, so the pre/post diff route stays dead.
- Some blocks have no `save()`-compatible correction at all (`aria-hidden` on a
  `core/group`), so `match` would be `null` for a real share of findings.
- **Unverified and the actual blocker:** whether a block validated in isolation gets the
  same verdict as in context. Most doubtful for deeply nested blocks whose parents are also
  invalid. Settle this before reopening.

Also note the `save()`-is-JavaScript-only argument was over-weighted originally: it rules
out PHP/server-side routes, which is what Gutenberg PR #82013 concerns, but this tool
already runs `save()` through block-runner in jsdom.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## Reopened — the blocking spike (wpbg-4n7) came back "sound"

Reopened per `wpbg-4n7`'s acceptance criteria, which specified reopening this bead if
block isolation turned out to be sound. It is.

### What was settled

A block sliced at its exact delimiter span and validated alone gets the same verdict and
reason as it does in its document — verified on 18 blocks across two fixtures with 0
divergences, and true *by construction*: `validateBlock` compares
`getSaveContent(blockType, block.attributes)` against `block.originalContent`, and `save()`
receives no block context. Nothing outside a block's own span feeds its validation.

Full detail: `handoff/2026-09-05-block-isolation-verdict-spike.md`.

### Cost figures (the original objection, now dead)

The ~12s-per-block estimate that justified closing this bead was measured before the
in-process adapter (`wpbg-km9`). Re-measured in one process:

| operation | cost |
|---|---|
| first call (jsdom + Gutenberg boot) | ~7.9s, paid once per process regardless |
| isolated `validate()` per block | median 9ms / 2ms across two fixtures; 8 blocks = 128ms total |
| isolated `canonicalize()` per block | 12ms and 34ms on the two repairable blocks tested |

Canonicalizing every invalid block in a file is fractions of a second, not ~48s.

### Per-block canonicalize actually works

Three invalid blocks from `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html`, canonicalized
alone:

| block | result |
|---|---|
| `core/paragraph` line 8 | **repaired**, 34ms — `style="margin-top:0;margin-bottom:0"` added; summary `1 valid, 0 invalid` |
| `core/paragraph` line 16 | **repaired**, 12ms — `style="margin-top:0;margin-bottom:1.25rem"` added |
| `core/group` line 6 | **not repaired** — `aria-hidden="true"` has no attribute to hold it |

Critically, the whole-document reformatting problem that made a pre/post diff useless
**disappears when the input is a single block**: there are no untouched sibling blocks to
be reindented, so the output is the corrected block and nothing else.

### Two new obstacles, neither known when this was closed

1. **Canonicalize is not byte-preserving.** The line-8 paragraph's numeric character
   references (`你好` and friends) came back as literal CJK/Cyrillic/Greek
   characters. Semantically equivalent; still a rewrite of content the user did not ask to
   change. A `match` field would need to either accept this or re-encode.
2. **Not every invalid block is repairable.** The `aria-hidden` group is the known case.
   `match` must be `null` for those, and the schema needs to distinguish "no correction
   exists" from "correction not attempted".

### Not yet decided

Whether `match` is worth having at all is still a design call — this bead is reopened
because its *stated blocker* is resolved, not because the feature has been re-approved.
`docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md` needs revisiting either way: its
cost-based reasoning is superseded, and the two obstacles above are what actually remain.
